tagline: The old Cherry Valley Turnpike over the Central New York hills.
intro: From LaFayette, US 20 drops into a deep valley and climbs back to the ridge at Pompey, then comes down to the south end of Cazenovia Lake. East of there it climbs into the high ground again past Morrisville, takes the name Cherry Valley Turnpike near Waterville and skirts the northern edge of the Catskills, valley views opening to the south, through Richfield Springs to Duanesburg, 108 miles on.

The turnpike was built around the turn of the 19th century to join Albany to Cherry Valley and later Cazenovia, and taverns and hotels lined it for the wagon trade. Dairy barns of Dutch and English build still stand along it, along with motor courts from the 1930s to the 1950s.

moments.title: Pompey
moments.text: Out of the valley at the Big Bend the road climbs five miles to the crest of the ridge, crossing NY 91 at 1,700 feet above the sea.

moments.title: Cazenovia
moments.text: In 1850 this village at the south end of Cazenovia Lake held the Fugitive Slave Convention, chaired by Frederick Douglass, days before the act it met to answer was passed.

moments.title: Sharon Springs
moments.text: In 1875 the New York Times reported a spring here so full of sulfur gas that its creek ran white as milk, and old shoes thrown in turned snowy white or deep black.
